newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes lower on dollar/yen movement.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes lower on dollar/yen movement.

text.p: The won closed lower on Wednesday in line with the dollar's strength against major currencies on the world market, dealers said.
They said the dollar climbed above the 893 won level when the U.S currency rose to 119.40 yen in Tokyo.
"The market opened gap up due to the dollar's strength against the yen," said a foreign bank dealer. The won opened at 892.00, even higher than yesterday's low of 890.60.
The won finished at 893.00, compared with Tuesday's close of 890.30. Dealers forecast Thursday's mid-rate would be pegged at 892.60 against 890.00 today.
A domestic bank dealer said affiliates of Samsung and Hyundai groups bought dollars in preparation of importer deal settlements, pulling down the local currency.
The won fell to the day low of 893.20 before the close on dollar short-covering by some major local banks.
"But the upside or downside of the dollar looked to be limited on fears of central bank interventions," said the local bank dealer.
The foreign bank dealer warned: "It'll be risky to have a lot of open positions when the domestic market is affected by external factors." -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
